*Explore operator and worker verbs in unusual orders with the nouns-and-verbs
  list, the test clock and a random sequence generator to discover sequences that leave jobs in
  states the spec does not allow.* Prediction (from reading the handlers): "every verb either does

  explorer writes (`exploration/experiments/05-sequence-it/walk.sh`: pick a noun, pick a verb, act,

Probe family: pairs and triples of verbs chosen for being unlikely (purge then enqueue-with-delay;
  pause, advance the clock an hour, resume; lease, purge, nack; cancel, retry); then the random walk
  for the rest of the budget, asserting `rules.md` after every step.

Budget: at most 60 minutes wall clock. Record elapsed reading/probing/writing.

content.content:
# Queuelet exploration protocol

An experiment teaches us about the inherited system by comparing a prediction with observation. Source reading is allowed and valuable; the register, proof scripts and SUT history are withheld. This document defines the local record and roles. It does not describe expected defects.

## Roles and export

The coordinator prepares a charter and an empty export directory. The seeder/fixer and explorer must be from different model families. Every experiment uses a fresh headless explorer. The reviewer independently checks the checkpoint and blindness boundary.

Export only the previous tag’s `books/explore-it/project`, `books/explore-it/exploration`, `books/explore-it/skills` and `books/explore-it/lessons`, preserving their relative paths. From the repository root, with the chosen tag and an existing empty destination:

```sh
git archive "$experiment_tag" books/explore-it/project books/explore-it/exploration books/explore-it/skills books/explore-it/lessons | tar -x -C "$export_dir"
```

The export has no `.git`, `PLAN.md`, `register/`, seeder proofs or hidden copy of repository history. Inspect its file list before dispatch. Existing experiment records, disclosed previous lessons and repro scripts may be present at later tags; they are prior knowledge, never a briefing about unfound targets. Keep the new charter and brief free of planted hints. The explorer can read any file in the export, including all source, and run the lab; it must not read outside the export or consult the originating checkout. Where external tools/services are necessary, their permitted use is specified in the brief rather than granting access to outside source or answer keys.

The committed `experiments/NN-<slug>/brief.md` names the export path, charter, relevant skill, this protocol, budget, permission profile and acceptance checks. It states the export-only reading rule and contains no information about what is planted. The coordinator supplies the charter; it is not assembled by the explorer from the plan.

## Before the probe

Each charter has one target, named resources/instruments and one kind of information:

```text
Explore <target> with <resources> to discover <information>.
I predict <observable behavior>.
Source: <spec line, code file:line, model cell, previous surprise or risk hypothesis>.
I would be wrong if <observable refutation>.
Budget: 60 minutes wall clock; planned reading / probing / writing split.
```

Write predictions and refutation conditions before executing the corresponding probe, including new hypotheses formed mid-run. A source reading is evidence for a prediction, not its confirmation. Separate should (named oracle), predicted (what code appears to do) and observed (what ran). Later observations can shape the next probe within this charter. Backlog adjacent questions as `#offcharter`; the explorer never widens the assignment.

The run budget includes reading, probing, resetting and writing. Track elapsed time and the actual reading/probing/writing split. No probe is worth losing the record to a time-out.

## During the run

Keep `experiments/NN-<slug>/notes.md` as timestamped entries. Use UTC timestamps and these tags:

| Tag | Record |
|---|---|
| `#read` | Source observation with file:line and its interpretation |
| `#hypothesis` | Id, source, prediction and refutation before the probe |
| `#obs` | Exact command, trimmed output and observed effects |
| `#surprise` | A discrepancy requiring characterization |
| `#bug` | Evidence and report link for an oracle violation |
| `#question` | An unresolved question or missing observation |
| `#offcharter` | Adjacent lead saved without expanding the target |

Retain dead ends, failed commands and timestamps. Trim repetitive output but retain evidence that determines the judgment. Preserve raw output or a linked artifact when trimming would lose meaning. Record fixture/reset identity, actors and relevant clock state. Read-only database observations are permitted; inject failures through lab/partner controls, container actions or documented clock controls, not hidden service paths or ad hoc source changes.

When no console answers a question, record a testability request with the question, missing signal, minimal hook and validation probe. The explorer proposes hooks; the fixer implements them in the separate fix stage.

## Characterize surprises

Every `#surprise` ends in a defect report or an explicit written reason it is not one. Isolate variables and reduce the reproduction. If it will not reproduce, preserve exact original state, vary one thing at a time, suspect timing and clock sources, and keep attempts and uncertainty in the log.

Reports under `defects/` contain:

- Title and tag/build seen at; link to the original observation.
- Exact minimal setup and steps, including actor, clock and fixture assumptions.
- Expected behavior with its named oracle: spec line, Never/Always rule, comparable system/standard or approximation with bounds.
- Observed behavior and evidence.
- Variables isolated, including what did not matter.
- Sibling check: where else the same cause could live, with file:line, or “none found.” Predictions about siblings must precede their probes.
- Severity with impact, and status: `open`, `fixed in lesson NN`, `won't fix: <why>` or `spec`.

The explorer writes reports in its own words with local provisional identifiers if necessary. The coordinator reconciles them with the hidden register: retain the planted `D##` id when matched; assign `U##` to an unplanned finding. Identifier reconciliation must not insert the register’s explanation into the explorer’s account.

## Close and score the run

Write `revealed.md` with charter status (`done`, `needs more` or `blocked`), elapsed time and reading/probing/writing split, what the system showed in plain words, model delta with file/cell links, unresolved uncertainties and next hypotheses. End with this score table, using actual counts and evidence links:

| Measure | Count | Evidence / counting basis |
|---|---|---|
| Hypotheses stated | | Distinct ids stated before probing |
| Hypotheses confirmed | | Predictions supported by the stated observation |
| Hypotheses refuted | | Stated refutation condition observed |
| Code-reading predictions contradicted by the running system | | Refuted subset whose recorded source was code |
| Defects found | | Distinct evidenced reports, excluding disclosure |
| Model cells filled | | Previously unobserved cells now supported by evidence |

Record hypotheses left `needs more` explicitly; confirmed plus refuted need not equal stated. Neither running a command nor adding an inferred diagram cell establishes observed coverage. Count a repeated observation once, and link separate defect findings even when one probe exposes several. A prediction of a defect can be confirmed while the product behavior violates its oracle; keep these judgments separate.

An experiment may need a second run with a narrowed charter. It closes after at most two runs. The coordinator discloses remaining planted misses in the lesson note under “What the experiment missed, and why,” and the fixer flags them `disclosed`. Never backfill these into the explorer’s notes, scores or finds. Preserve out-of-order and unplanned discoveries as they happened.

## Backlog and living models

`hypotheses.md` retains every proposed hypothesis: id, statement/prediction, source, refutation, intended probe/experiment and status (`open` or `experiment NN: confirmed|refuted|needs more`). Keep original statements when updating outcomes.

Models under `models/` grow from observations: `map.md`, `nouns-verbs.md`, `variables.md`, `rules.md`, `entities.md`, `states.md`, `ecosystem.md` and, after evidence supports cause analysis, `causes.md`. Label inference and uncertainty. Later experiments revise earlier models; their diffs are evidence of learning. In a cause-prediction run, commit or timestamp the predicted-defects table before running the confirming probes.

## Handoff and verification

The coordinator commits experiment artifacts as produced, formatting only. Fixes belong in a separate fresh fixer run from the seeder’s family, using the reports as brief. The fixer changes only named findings, adds a regression check per defect under `project/test/checks/` and black-box repro scripts under `project/lab/repro/`, and writes the lesson note. A spec silence also needs a spec line and the coordinator’s one-line decision in the fix commit body. The lesson tag points at the fix commit. Fix history remains separate from the experiment record.

`make verify LESSON=NN` resets and runs that experiment’s repros and checks. Its final verdict is `FIXED AND CHECKED:` after repair or `DEFECTS REPRODUCED:` against the earlier version. Repros report `PRESENT:` or `ABSENT:` per defect; thresholds are binary and may not be weakened to hide a defect. `REF=<tag>` uses the current repros against earlier SUT code. `make checks` runs all regression checks; `make test` runs unit tests. `make dwell LESSON=NN` optionally shows present/absent across earlier tags; its result does not gate the verdict. Lesson 00 uses `BASELINE HOLDS:`.

Lesson notes include actual found/missed/found-early/unplanned outcomes, the score and before/after evidence. Review checks that previous-version repros still reproduce the finding, models match evidence and no answer key leaked into the brief or export.

## Source and local adaptations

Hendrickson, [*Explore It!*](https://pragprog.com/titles/ehxta/explore-it/) (2013): 1.1–1.3, 2.1–2.4 and 2.6, Chapter 3, 10.4, 11.5–11.6 and 13.3. Section numbering checked against the publisher’s contents extract; detailed text review remains pending. Blind exports, split agent roles, explicit prediction/refutation lines, score format and the two-commit lesson are this repo’s implementation of the approved plan, not claims of prescribed book formats.

# Probe sequences and states

Draft for execution against queuelet. In this arc follow [the protocol](../../exploration/PROTOCOL.md); operate within the export and assigned charter.

## When to use

A status-bearing object, retry/cancel/timeout protocol or operator/worker interaction.

## Inputs

Nouns/verbs, spec lifecycle and rules, source guards, fixtures, relevant actors/clocks and charter.

## Procedure

1. List nouns and verbs. Select unlikely pairs/triples, repetitions and interruptions. Predict effects before driving each sequence; record starting state and actor identity.
2. Check agreed rules after every step. For random walks retain seed, operation log, preconditions and observations for replay. A skipped operation is not coverage.
3. Derive states/events from spec and observation, including background actions and timeouts. Diagram them and label inferred states and unobserved arrows.
4. Expand into state × event cells with should (named oracle), predicted (source/guards), observed and evidence. Keep unknown distinct from forbidden. Include ownership/actor context when it changes behavior.
5. Drive rejected and undefined cells, prioritizing disagreement between should and predicted. Use multiple actors or controlled timing where needed; demonstrate prerequisite state instead of assuming a sleep reached it.
6. Reduce failing walks to shortest explanatory sequences, preserving needed identities/timing. Update the model and reports. The fixer turns agreed cells into model-based checks; the explorer does not silently repair the SUT.

## Output

Sequence grid, replayable walk log, state/event table with should/predicted/observed; separate filled, untried and blocked cells; minimal failures and model delta.

## Source

Elisabeth Hendrickson, [*Explore It!*](https://pragprog.com/titles/ehxta/explore-it/) (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2013), sections 6.1, 6.2 and 8.1–8.4. Section numbering checked against the publisher’s contents extract. This draft adapts the approved plan’s chapter map; detailed source-text review is pending. The procedure and local record formats are repo guidance, not quotations from the book.

## Worked example

Pending real experiments. E05 will provide a walker and E07 a state table. Litefleet’s database lifecycle is a second target after both arcs. No transitions are pre-filled. No run results or scores are claimed yet.

# Queuelet service contract

Queuelet stores jobs durably in PostgreSQL and distributes them to workers.
A namespace contains queues, workers and schedules. A bearer API key selects a
namespace; an administrative key may inspect namespace statistics.

## Authentication and responses

Every `/v1/` request requires `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
A namespace key accesses only its namespace's resources.
The health and metrics endpoints are public.
JSON commands use `Content-Type: application/json`.
Errors have the form `{"error":{"code":"…","message":"…"}}` and a 4xx or 5xx
HTTP status. Successful reads and mutations return 200 unless stated otherwise.
Creation returns 201. Deletion returns 204. A missing resource returns 404.
A command incompatible with the current state returns 409.
A path no route serves is 404 and a method a route does not accept is 405, both
in the same error form.
Unknown fields and invalid enum values should be rejected as invalid commands.
A command body is exactly one JSON object in UTF-8. Trailing data, invalid UTF-8
and member names that match a documented field only when case is ignored are
rejected with 400 `invalid_json`.
Every seconds-valued field and `max_attempts` accepts at most 2147483647.
A `delay_seconds` (enqueue or nack) is never negative; a negative value is 400.

## Queues

`POST /v1/queues` creates a queue with a unique name within the namespace.
Names use 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. Only a taken name
is a 409 conflict; an invalid or out-of-range setting is 400.
Configuration defaults are `lease_seconds:30`, `max_attempts:3`,
`backoff:{kind:"exponential",base_seconds:5}`, `retention_hours:24`.
Lease duration and maximum attempts must be positive; retention hours range from
0 through 1000000.
Backoff kind is `linear` or `exponential`; the base is a nonnegative number
of seconds. Failed jobs retry with exponential backoff from `base_seconds`
or linear backoff when configured. An optional `backoff.max_seconds`, at least
`base_seconds`, caps each wait. Without it each wait is capped at 3600 seconds,
or at `base_seconds` when that is larger. A computed wait never overflows: it is capped
at 2147483647 seconds, so a retry is never scheduled before the failure.
An optional `webhook:{url,secret}` receives terminal notifications.

`GET /v1/queues` lists the namespace's queues.
`GET /v1/queues/{name}` reads configuration.
`PATCH /v1/queues/{name}` updates lease duration, maximum attempts, retention
or webhook settings. Existing jobs retain their maximum-attempt setting.
Omitted members keep their value, inside `webhook` as well: a secret-only PATCH
keeps the URL and a URL-only PATCH keeps the secret.
`DELETE /v1/queues/{name}` removes a queue; owned jobs and schedules must not
become orphaned. Callers must handle a conflict for a nonempty queue.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/pause` prevents new leases and scheduled deliveries.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/resume` allows work again. Missed periodic ticks should
not create an unbounded burst of catch-up jobs.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/purge` removes all pending jobs: scheduled, queued and retry_wait.

## Jobs

`POST /v1/queues/{name}/jobs` accepts `kind`, a JSON object `payload`, and
optional `priority`, `delay_seconds`, `run_at`, `max_attempts`, `idempotency_key`.
Kind is required. Priority ranges from 0 through 9 and defaults to 5.
Payload values are delivered to workers without loss of numeric precision.
Choose either delay in seconds or an RFC3339 `run_at`, never both.
A job due now is `queued`; a future job is `scheduled`.
The service promotes due jobs to `queued`.
A queue's maximum-attempt setting is copied to each new job unless overridden.
Repeated use of an idempotency key within a queue returns the original job.

`POST /v1/queues/{name}/jobs:batch` accepts `{"jobs":[…]}` with 1–500 jobs.
An empty or oversized batch is invalid and returns 400 without insertion.
A batch is atomic: an invalid element leaves none of its new jobs stored.
It returns `{"ids":[…]}` after accepted jobs are stored.
`GET /v1/queues/{name}/jobs` supports state, kind, limit and cursor filters.
The limit defaults to 100 and is at most 500. The returned next cursor can
be used to continue through increasing job ids.
Valid state filters are `scheduled`, `queued`, `leased`, `retry_wait`,
`succeeded`, `dead` and `cancelled`.
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}` returns the current job, payload, result and last error.
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}/attempts` returns completed attempts in numeric order.
Attempt `n` numbers every execution of the job and is never reused, across
operator retries too; the lease's `attempt` counts toward `max_attempts`.
`DELETE /v1/jobs/{id}` removes a terminal job.

## Worker protocol

`POST /v1/workers` takes a name and an array of supported kinds.
It returns a worker id and token.
`DELETE /v1/workers/{id}` deregisters the worker and releases its active leases.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/lease` takes `worker_id` and `max_jobs` (1–100).
Only jobs with a kind supported by that worker are eligible.
Leasing is atomic; concurrent workers cannot acquire the same lease.
Higher priorities run first. Within a priority, jobs run FIFO by creation order.
The response includes job id, kind, payload, attempt, lease token and expiry.

A worker sends `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/heartbeat` with the lease token and positive
`extend_seconds` to extend its lease.
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/ack` supplies the lease token and result and completes work.
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/nack` supplies the lease token, an error and optional retry
boolean (default true) or a `delay_seconds` override.
Only the current lease holder may complete or extend a job. A lease ends at its
`lease_expires_at`: from that instant heartbeat, ack and nack are 409, whether or
not the background loop has released the job yet. There is no grace period.
Ack moves a leased job to `succeeded`.
Nack with retry moves a job to `retry_wait`; when due it becomes `queued`.
A failed job reaches `dead` when its maximum attempts are exhausted, or when
nacked with retry false. No job may execute more than its maximum attempts.
An expired lease records an unsuccessful attempt and releases the job for retry
unless the maximum attempts have been exhausted.

## Operator actions and retention

`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` cancels a nonterminal job.
A cancelled job is never run.
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/retry` permits an operator to retry a dead job, resets its
attempt count and makes it immediately available.
Succeeded and cancelled jobs cannot be retried.
Terminal jobs are deleted after `retention_hours`.
The API returns complete stored results and errors.

## Schedules

`POST /v1/schedules` takes name, queue, kind, payload, cron, timezone and enabled.
Cron uses five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week.
Time zones use IANA identifiers, defaulting to UTC.
Schedule times follow the named zone's local civil time, including offset changes.
The enabled flag defaults to true; disabled schedules do not enqueue jobs.
`GET /v1/schedules` lists schedules; `GET /v1/schedules/{id}` reads one.
`PATCH /v1/schedules/{id}` updates cron, timezone or enabled status; the next fire
must reflect the current configuration.
`DELETE /v1/schedules/{id}` removes it.
`POST /v1/schedules/{id}/run` enqueues one immediate execution.

## Notifications and operations

Terminal transitions produce a webhook outbox entry when the queue has a URL.
The entry includes job id, state, result and last error.
Notification results preserve their JSON type; results and errors are complete.
Each POST carries `X-Queuelet-Signature`, a hex HMAC-SHA256 over the body using
the configured secret. Delivery is successful only on a 2xx response.
Failed notifications are retried. Delivery is at least once.

`GET /v1/queues/{name}/stats` and `GET /v1/namespaces/{name}/stats` expose counts
by exact state, oldest queued age in seconds and completed jobs in the last hour.
Queued age uses the later of creation and readiness, over queued rows only.
A job released by lease expiry or worker deletion becomes ready at the release.
`GET /health` returns service health; `GET /metrics` returns minimal text metrics.
The background loop promotes scheduled jobs, expires leases, fires cron schedules,
sweeps retention and delivers webhooks. It should recover after a database restart. Webhook latency must not block core
lifecycle progress. Health reports database availability and loop degradation;
an unavailable authentication store returns 503 rather than invalid credentials.


### Notification destinations, snapshots and acknowledgement

Queue create/PATCH rejects malformed or non-HTTP(S) webhook URLs with 400;
an empty URL disables future notification snapshots. Each completed job's outbox
row retains its destination, secret and body. Configuration edits apply to future
snapshots; deleting a job does not erase pending deliveries. A malformed legacy
row is counted as a failed attempt and rescheduled independently, so it does not
stop later rows.

"Delivered" means queuelet received a 2xx response before its two-second HTTP
client deadline. A timeout does not reveal whether the receiver completed its
side effect. Failed attempts retry after five seconds; duplicates are possible,
including when the receiver processed a timed-out request. This lesson adds no
attempt cap, dead-letter state, timeout knob or backoff policy for notifications.

# Rules (named oracles)

Authority: SPEC.md unless stated. Scope: v0-inherited. Observation column cites E01 notes/defects.

| Rule | Authority | Scope | E01 observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 Namespace key accesses only its namespace's resources | SPEC Auth | all /v1 | Violated for job-id endpoints (F03); holds for queues, schedules, workers, lease worker check |
| R2 Only the current lease holder may complete or extend | SPEC Worker | ack/nack/heartbeat | Violated ack (F01), nack (F02); holds heartbeat (H31) |
| R3 No job executes more than max_attempts | SPEC Worker (Never rule) | nack, expiry | Violated (F04, F05) |
| R4 Expired lease records an unsuccessful attempt | SPEC Worker | Loop/Expire | Violated (F05) |
| R5 Cancelled job is never run | SPEC Operator (Never) | cancel + any later verb | Violated via nack (F02) |
| R6 Succeeded/cancelled cannot be retried | SPEC Operator | retry | Violated (F06) |
| R7 Missing resource → 404; state conflict → 409; errors 4xx/5xx | SPEC Responses | all | Violated: lease unknown worker 200 (F21); delete missing queue 204 (F15); DB outage → 401 (F14) |
| R8 Unknown fields / invalid enums rejected | SPEC Responses | all bodies, filters | Violated (F20) |
| R9 Names ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_-]; priority 0–9; positive limits | SPEC Queues/Jobs | create, patch | Violated (F19) |
| R10 Payload numeric precision preserved | SPEC Jobs | enqueue → lease/GET | Violated (F17) |
| R11 Batch 1–500, else 400 without insertion | SPEC Jobs | batch | Violated (F16) |
| R12 FIFO by creation order within priority | SPEC Worker | lease | Violated on same-second ties (F23); held for 40 untouched jobs (H22) |
| R13 Delete queue: no orphans, conflict if nonempty | SPEC Queues | DELETE queue | Violated (F15) |
| R14 Pause stops scheduled deliveries; no unbounded catch-up | SPEC Queues | Fire | Pause holds; catch-up violated (F24) |
| R15 PATCH schedule: next fire reflects config; disabled never enqueues | SPEC Schedules | PATCH, Fire | Violated (F07, F09) |
| R16 Civil time incl. offset changes | SPEC Schedules | Next | Violated via harness (F27) |
| R17 Webhook HMAC over body; success only 2xx; retried; data agrees or marks truncation | SPEC Notifications | Ship, Notify | Violated (F10, F11, F12); transport-error retry holds (H34) |

# 04 — Judge it: write the oracles down, then break them

An output is only wrong against something. This experiment wrote that something down first: thirteen
Never/Always rules for a job queue, each with its authority (a spec line, an approximation, or a
comparable system), the line of code that should enforce it, and the observation that would break it.
Then it tried to break each one. Eight held. Five broke, and none of the five was a defect the plan had
put here.

The source is Hendrickson, *Explore It!* (2013), Chapter 5: 5.1 "Never and Always", 5.2 "Alternative
Resources", 5.3 "Approximations"; and 10.3 on status codes versus bodies. These citations follow the
approved [chapter map](../PLAN.md#22-chapter-map-kept-sections-only); the builder did not check them
against the book text.

## What the blind experiment learned

[The original record](../exploration/experiments/04-judge-it/revealed.md) is unchanged from the
experiment commit. The explorer stated 16 hypotheses, confirmed 15 and refuted 1: the charter's own
prediction, "the code honours every rule on my list". That was the one code-reading prediction the
running system contradicted. It filed 5 reports and filled 18 model cells, in about 15 minutes of a
60-minute budget.

The record shows a change in how the explorer reads. Before any probe it wrote the rules table in
[`models/rules.md`](../exploration/models/rules.md) (R31–R43). For each rule it wrote the enforcing line
from the source, and for five of them it wrote down in advance that the line was missing: no lower bound
on `delay_seconds`, no `lease_expires_at` in the worker guards, no key on `attempts`, `run_at` left alone
on release, and no `fail()` in front of the mux. All five predictions came true. In each case the
rule told the reader which line to look for, and the line was not there.

| Classification | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Expected here, found early | D09 off-by-one retries, D10 stats counts, D11 same-second FIFO, D25 lease error with 200: all found and fixed in E01. E04 re-probed D09–D11 as R32, R34 and R33, and they held. D25's route was not re-probed; `TestL01D25` still passes |
| Spec silence, resolved here | A1, no default backoff cap: measured (30.34 days at attempt 20) and raised as owner question Q-E04-1, **not blind** (see below) |
| Found as new in E04 | U19–U23 (below) |
| Missed / disclosed | none: no planted defect is left for this experiment |

**A1 was not a blind find.** The lesson 03 note, which is in every later export, says that A1 "(a
default backoff cap) stays with E04". The explorer read it, cited it, measured the 30-day wait and
handed the decision to the owner. It judged the wait compliant with the spec as written, since the only
stated bound is the 68-year overflow cap. That judgement is right, which is why A1 is a spec silence and
not a bug. Naming a register id in an exported note was a leak, though. From lesson 04 on, notes describe
open silences without saying which experiment the plan assigned them to.

**The comparable systems did their job without becoming requirements.** SQS FIFO orders by sequence
number, not by a timestamp, so the explorer could frame a backward clock step as a FIFO risk (H-E04-08)
without calling it a bug. SQS's `ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage` counts age from the original send. That
is the opposite of the reading behind E04-F05, so the report says plainly that its oracle depends on what
this spec means by "readiness". The explorer recalled both systems' behaviour from memory and marked it
"not verified in this run".

## The five faults, with pointers into `explore-it/lesson-03`

| ID | Report | Where it lived | What happened | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U19 | [E04-F01](../exploration/defects/E04-F01-unmatched-route-errors-not-json.md) | `internal/api/api.go:172` hands every authenticated request to `ServeMux`; only handlers call `fail()` | `PUT /v1/queues` → 405 `text/plain` "Method Not Allowed"; `GET /v1/nope` → "404 page not found" | R36 an error is always 4xx/5xx *in the error form* |
| U20 | [E04-F02](../exploration/defects/E04-F02-attempt-history-after-retry-ambiguous.md) | `ack.go:14`, `nack.go:30` insert `n = attempts`; `operator.go:13` resets `attempts` | after dead → retry → ack: `n=1 failed, n=1 succeeded, n=2 failed`; two executions share `n=1` | R38 one row per execution, numeric order = execution order |
| U21 | [E04-F03](../exploration/defects/E04-F03-negative-delay-wraps-and-precedes-failure.md) | `internal/api/jobs.go:67`, `enqueue.go:55` check only `> MaxSeconds` | nack `delay_seconds: -5` scheduled the retry 5 s before the failure; `-9223372037` wrapped to the year 2322 | R35 a retry comes after the failure, within a bound |
| U22 | [E04-F04](../exploration/defects/E04-F04-expired-lease-honoured-until-sweep.md) | `ack.go:10`, `nack.go:14`, `jobs.go:97` guard on token and state, never on `lease_expires_at` | a heartbeat sent just after expiry, before the 1 s sweep, revived the lease (5/5); one tick later the same request got 409 | R39 an expired lease is not current |
| U23 | [E04-F05](../exploration/defects/E04-F05-queued-age-counts-leased-time.md) | `stats.go:18` uses `GREATEST(created_at, run_at)`; `expire.go:41` and `internal/api/jobs.go:126` requeue without touching `run_at` | a job released by expiry reported `oldest_queued_age` 600 s; by worker deletion, 100 s | R40 queued age measures waiting since the job became ready |

U21 is the other half of U13: lesson 03 bounded `delay_seconds` from above only. U23 is a release path
that U08's "later of creation and readiness" (lesson 01) never reached. In both cases an earlier fix
asked part of the question, and here a written rule asked all of it.

## The patch

About 90 lines under `project/`, excluding instruments; the lines that matter:

- **One error form for unmatched requests** (`internal/api/api.go`, `unmatched`). The auth wrapper asks
  `m.Handler(r)` which pattern would serve the request. If none would, it runs the mux's own 404/405
  handler into `statusOnly`, which keeps the status and the `Allow` header and drops the plain-text
  body. Then it writes `not_found` or `method_not_allowed` with `fail()`.
- **History that survives a retry** (`ack.go`, `nack.go`, `expire.go`). Each new attempt row is
  numbered `(SELECT count(*)+1 FROM attempts WHERE job_id=$1)` instead of copying `jobs.attempts`. The
  budget counter still resets on retry, as the spec says; the history no longer does.
- **No negative delays** (`internal/api/jobs.go`, `enqueue.go`). `delay_seconds < 0` is 400 next to
  the existing upper bound.
- **A lease ends when it says it ends** (`ack.go`, `nack.go`, `jobs.go` `Heartbeat`). Each guard gains
  `AND lease_expires_at > $now`. The sweep still records the expired attempt; it just no longer decides
  whether a late worker wins.
- **Release resets readiness** (`expire.go`, `deleteWorker`). `run_at = now` when a leased job goes

# 04 — Judge it: write the oracles down, then break them

An output is only wrong against something. This experiment wrote that something down first: thirteen
Never/Always rules for a job queue, each with its authority (a spec line, an approximation, or a
comparable system), the line of code that should enforce it, and the observation that would break it.
Then it tried to break each one. Eight held. Five broke, and none of the five was a defect the plan had
put here.

The source is Hendrickson, *Explore It!* (2013), Chapter 5: 5.1 "Never and Always", 5.2 "Alternative
Resources", 5.3 "Approximations"; and 10.3 on status codes versus bodies. These citations follow the
approved [chapter map](../PLAN.md#22-chapter-map-kept-sections-only); the builder did not check them
against the book text.

## What the blind experiment learned

[The original record](../exploration/experiments/04-judge-it/revealed.md) is unchanged from the
experiment commit. The explorer stated 16 hypotheses, confirmed 15 and refuted 1: the charter's own
prediction, "the code honours every rule on my list". That was the one code-reading prediction the
running system contradicted. It filed 5 reports and filled 18 model cells, in about 15 minutes of a
60-minute budget.

The record shows a change in how the explorer reads. Before any probe it wrote the rules table in
[`models/rules.md`](../exploration/models/rules.md) (R31–R43). For each rule it wrote the enforcing line
from the source, and for five of them it wrote down in advance that the line was missing: no lower bound
on `delay_seconds`, no `lease_expires_at` in the worker guards, no key on `attempts`, `run_at` left alone
on release, and no `fail()` in front of the mux. All five predictions came true. In each case the
rule told the reader which line to look for, and the line was not there.

| Classification | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Expected here, found early | D09 off-by-one retries, D10 stats counts, D11 same-second FIFO, D25 lease error with 200: all found and fixed in E01. E04 re-probed D09–D11 as R32, R34 and R33, and they held. D25's route was not re-probed; `TestL01D25` still passes |
| Spec silence, resolved here | A1, no default backoff cap: measured (30.34 days at attempt 20) and raised as owner question Q-E04-1, **not blind** (see below) |
| Found as new in E04 | U19–U23 (below) |
| Missed / disclosed | none: no planted defect is left for this experiment |

**A1 was not a blind find.** The lesson 03 note, which is in every later export, says that A1 "(a
default backoff cap) stays with E04". The explorer read it, cited it, measured the 30-day wait and
handed the decision to the owner. It judged the wait compliant with the spec as written, since the only
stated bound is the 68-year overflow cap. That judgement is right, which is why A1 is a spec silence and
not a bug. Naming a register id in an exported note was a leak, though. From lesson 04 on, notes describe
open silences without saying which experiment the plan assigned them to.

**The comparable systems did their job without becoming requirements.** SQS FIFO orders by sequence
number, not by a timestamp, so the explorer could frame a backward clock step as a FIFO risk (H-E04-08)
without calling it a bug. SQS's `ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage` counts age from the original send. That
is the opposite of the reading behind E04-F05, so the report says plainly that its oracle depends on what
this spec means by "readiness". The explorer recalled both systems' behaviour from memory and marked it
"not verified in this run".

## The five faults, with pointers into `explore-it/lesson-03`

| ID | Report | Where it lived | What happened | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U19 | [E04-F01](../exploration/defects/E04-F01-unmatched-route-errors-not-json.md) | `internal/api/api.go:172` hands every authenticated request to `ServeMux`; only handlers call `fail()` | `PUT /v1/queues` → 405 `text/plain` "Method Not Allowed"; `GET /v1/nope` → "404 page not found" | R36 an error is always 4xx/5xx *in the error form* |
| U20 | [E04-F02](../exploration/defects/E04-F02-attempt-history-after-retry-ambiguous.md) | `ack.go:14`, `nack.go:30` insert `n = attempts`; `operator.go:13` resets `attempts` | after dead → retry → ack: `n=1 failed, n=1 succeeded, n=2 failed`; two executions share `n=1` | R38 one row per execution, numeric order = execution order |
| U21 | [E04-F03](../exploration/defects/E04-F03-negative-delay-wraps-and-precedes-failure.md) | `internal/api/jobs.go:67`, `enqueue.go:55` check only `> MaxSeconds` | nack `delay_seconds: -5` scheduled the retry 5 s before the failure; `-9223372037` wrapped to the year 2322 | R35 a retry comes after the failure, within a bound |
| U22 | [E04-F04](../exploration/defects/E04-F04-expired-lease-honoured-until-sweep.md) | `ack.go:10`, `nack.go:14`, `jobs.go:97` guard on token and state, never on `lease_expires_at` | a heartbeat sent just after expiry, before the 1 s sweep, revived the lease (5/5); one tick later the same request got 409 | R39 an expired lease is not current |
| U23 | [E04-F05](../exploration/defects/E04-F05-queued-age-counts-leased-time.md) | `stats.go:18` uses `GREATEST(created_at, run_at)`; `expire.go:41` and `internal/api/jobs.go:126` requeue without touching `run_at` | a job released by expiry reported `oldest_queued_age` 600 s; by worker deletion, 100 s | R40 queued age measures waiting since the job became ready |

U21 is the other half of U13: lesson 03 bounded `delay_seconds` from above only. U23 is a release path
that U08's "later of creation and readiness" (lesson 01) never reached. In both cases an earlier fix
asked part of the question, and here a written rule asked all of it.

## The patch

About 90 lines under `project/`, excluding instruments; the lines that matter:

- **One error form for unmatched requests** (`internal/api/api.go`, `unmatched`). The auth wrapper asks
  `m.Handler(r)` which pattern would serve the request. If none would, it runs the mux's own 404/405
  handler into `statusOnly`, which keeps the status and the `Allow` header and drops the plain-text
  body. Then it writes `not_found` or `method_not_allowed` with `fail()`.
- **History that survives a retry** (`ack.go`, `nack.go`, `expire.go`). Each new attempt row is
  numbered `(SELECT count(*)+1 FROM attempts WHERE job_id=$1)` instead of copying `jobs.attempts`. The
  budget counter still resets on retry, as the spec says; the history no longer does.
- **No negative delays** (`internal/api/jobs.go`, `enqueue.go`). `delay_seconds < 0` is 400 next to
  the existing upper bound.
- **A lease ends when it says it ends** (`ack.go`, `nack.go`, `jobs.go` `Heartbeat`). Each guard gains
  `AND lease_expires_at > $now`. The sweep still records the expired attempt; it just no longer decides
  whether a late worker wins.
- **Release resets readiness** (`expire.go`, `deleteWorker`). `run_at = now` when a leased job goes

name: queuelet
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: queuelet
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: queuelet
      POSTGRES_DB: queuelet
    ports: ["${QUEUELET_PG_PORT:-15433}:5432"]
    healthcheck:
      test: [CMD-SHELL, "pg_isready -U queuelet"]
      interval: 1s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30
    volumes: ["data:/var/lib/postgresql/data"]
  api:
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: deploy/Dockerfile
    image: queuelet:${QUEUELET_IMAGE_TAG:-local}
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://queuelet:queuelet@postgres:5432/queuelet?sslmode=disable
      QUEUELET_TEST_CLOCK: "1"
    ports: ["${QUEUELET_API_PORT:-18200}:8200"]
    depends_on:
      postgres: {condition: service_healthy}
  hooksink:
    image: queuelet:${QUEUELET_IMAGE_TAG:-local}
    command: hooksink
    ports: ["${QUEUELET_HOOK_PORT:-18201}:8201"]
    environment: {WEBHOOK_SECRET: report-secret}
  worker-a:
    image: queuelet:${QUEUELET_IMAGE_TAG:-local}
    command: worker
    restart: on-failure
    environment:
      QUEUELET_URL: http://api:8200
      QUEUELET_KEY: acme-key
      WORKER_NAME: worker-a
      WORKER_QUEUE: emails
    depends_on: [api]
  worker-b:
    image: queuelet:${QUEUELET_IMAGE_TAG:-local}
    command: worker
    restart: on-failure
    environment:
      QUEUELET_URL: http://api:8200
      QUEUELET_KEY: acme-key
      WORKER_NAME: worker-b
      WORKER_QUEUE: reports
    depends_on: [api]
volumes:
  data:

E=/tmp/explore-it-experiment-05/books/explore-it/exploration/experiments/05-sequence-it; cat > $E/tools/pairs.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# E05 pair/triple probes P1-P8. Usage: bash pairs.sh P1 [P2 ...]  (prints commands and outputs; tee into results)
source "$(dirname "$0")/e05env.sh"
run() { echo "\$ $*"; "$@"; }
jget() { sql "select id,state,attempts,max_attempts,run_at,created_at,finished_at,leased_by,lease_token is not null as tok,lease_expires_at,last_error from jobs where id=$1"; }
mkq() { api POST /v1/queues -d "{\"name\":\"$1\"${2:+,$2}}"; }
wk() { api POST /v1/workers -d "{\"name\":\"$1\",\"kinds\":[\"k\"]}" | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .worker_id; }
lease1() { api POST /v1/queues/$1/lease -d "{\"worker_id\":$2,\"max_jobs\":1}"; }
P1() { echo "== P1 purge then enqueue-with-delay (idempotency key) $(ts)"
  run mkq p1
  run api POST /v1/queues/p1/jobs -d '{"kind":"k","delay_seconds":60,"idempotency_key":"K1"}'
  run api POST /v1/queues/p1/purge
  run api POST /v1/queues/p1/jobs -d '{"kind":"k","delay_seconds":60,"idempotency_key":"K1"}'
  run sql "select id,state,idempotency_key from jobs where queue_id=(select id from queues where name='p1')"; }
P2() { echo "== P2 pause, advance clock 1h, resume $(ts)"
  run mkq p2
  W=$(wk p2w); echo "worker $W"
  run api POST /v1/queues/p2/jobs -d '{"kind":"k","delay_seconds":60}'
  run api POST /v1/schedules -d '{"name":"p2s","queue":"p2","kind":"k","payload":{},"cron":"* * * * *"}'
  run api POST /v1/queues/p2/pause
  run adm POST /admin/clock -d '{"action":"advance","seconds":3600}'
  sleep 3
  run sql "select id,state,run_at,created_at from jobs where queue_id=(select id from queues where name='p2') order by id"
  run sql "select id,next_run_at,last_run_at from schedules where name='p2s'"
  run lease1 p2 $W
  sleep 2
  run api POST /v1/queues/p2/resume
  sleep 3
  run sql "select id,state,run_at,created_at from jobs where queue_id=(select id from queues where name='p2') order by id"
  run api POST /v1/queues/p2/lease -d "{\"worker_id\":$W,\"max_jobs\":10}"
  run sql "select id,next_run_at,last_run_at from schedules where name='p2s'"; }
P3() { echo "== P3 lease, purge, nack $(ts)"
  run mkq p3
  W=$(wk p3w)
  J=$(api POST /v1/queues/p3/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id); echo "job $J"
  L=$(lease1 p3 $W); echo "$L"; T=$(echo "$L" | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r '.jobs[0].lease_token')
  run api POST /v1/queues/p3/purge
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$J/nack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"$T\",\"error\":\"after purge\"}"
  run jget $J
  run api POST /v1/queues/p3/purge
  run jget $J; }
P4() { echo "== P4 cancel->retry, dead->cancel, succeeded->retry $(ts)"
  run mkq p4 '"max_attempts":1'
  W=$(wk p4w)
  A=$(api POST /v1/queues/p4/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$A/cancel
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$A/retry
  B=$(api POST /v1/queues/p4/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  T=$(lease1 p4 $W | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r '.jobs[0].lease_token')
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$B/nack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"$T\",\"error\":\"x\"}"
  run jget $B
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$B/cancel
  C=$(api POST /v1/queues/p4/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  T=$(lease1 p4 $W | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r '.jobs[0].lease_token')
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$C/ack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"$T\",\"result\":1}"
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$C/retry
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$C/cancel; }
P5() { echo "== P5 lease, cancel: lease fields $(ts)"
  run mkq p5
  W=$(wk p5w)
  J=$(api POST /v1/queues/p5/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  run lease1 p5 $W
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$J/cancel
  run jget $J
  run api GET /v1/jobs/$J; }
P6() { echo "== P6 lease, delete worker, lease ... (max_attempts 2) $(ts)"
  run mkq p6 '"max_attempts":2'
  J=$(api POST /v1/queues/p6/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id); echo "job $J"
  for i in 1 2 3 4; do
    W=$(wk p6w$i)
    L=$(lease1 p6 $W); echo "lease by $W: $L"
    T=$(echo "$L" | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r '.jobs[0].lease_token')
    run api DELETE /v1/workers/$W
    run api POST /v1/jobs/$J/heartbeat -d "{\"lease_token\":\"$T\",\"extend_seconds\":30}"
    run jget $J
  done
  run api GET /v1/jobs/$J/attempts
  run sql "select event,worker,attempt from job_events where job_id=$J order by id"; }
P7() { echo "== P7 lease (lease_seconds 2, max 1), pause, expiry while paused $(ts)"
  run mkq p7 '"lease_seconds":2,"max_attempts":1'
  W=$(wk p7w)
  J=$(api POST /v1/queues/p7/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  run lease1 p7 $W
  run api POST /v1/queues/p7/pause
  sleep 4
  run jget $J
  run api GET /v1/jobs/$J/attempts; }
P8() { echo "== P8 cancel scheduled / cancel retry_wait, then time passes $(ts)"
  run mkq p8 '"backoff":{"kind":"linear","base_seconds":30}'
  W=$(wk p8w)
  A=$(api POST /v1/queues/p8/jobs -d '{"kind":"k","delay_seconds":30}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  B=$(api POST /v1/queues/p8/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  T=$(lease1 p8 $W | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r '.jobs[0].lease_token')
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$B/nack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"$T\",\"error\":\"x\"}"
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$A/cancel
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$B/cancel
  run adm POST /admin/clock -d '{"action":"advance","seconds":120}'
  sleep 3
  run jget $A; run jget $B
  run lease1 p8 $W; }
for p in "$@"; do $p; done
EOF
source $E/tools/e05env.sh; bash $E/tools/pairs.sh P1 P3 P4 P5 2>&1 | tee $RES/p1-p5.txt
input.description: Write pair probe script and run P1,P3,P4,P5

  W=$(wk p2w); echo "worker $W"
  run api POST /v1/queues/p2/jobs -d '{"kind":"k","delay_seconds":60}'
  run api POST /v1/schedules -d '{"name":"p2s","queue":"p2","kind":"k","payload":{},"cron":"* * * * *"}'
  run api POST /v1/queues/p2/pause
  run adm POST /admin/clock -d '{"action":"advance","seconds":3600}'
  sleep 3
  run sql "select id,state,run_at,created_at from jobs where queue_id=(select id from queues where name='p2') order by id"
  run sql "select id,next_run_at,last_run_at from schedules where name='p2s'"
  run lease1 p2 $W
  sleep 2
  run api POST /v1/queues/p2/resume
  sleep 3
  run sql "select id,state,run_at,created_at from jobs where queue_id=(select id from queues where name='p2') order by id"
  run api POST /v1/queues/p2/lease -d "{\"worker_id\":$W,\"max_jobs\":10}"
  run sql "select id,next_run_at,last_run_at from schedules where name='p2s'"; }
P3() { echo "== P3 lease, purge, nack $(ts)"
  run mkq p3
  W=$(wk p3w)
  J=$(api POST /v1/queues/p3/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id); echo "job $J"
  L=$(lease1 p3 $W); echo "$L"; T=$(echo "$L" | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r '.jobs[0].lease_token')
  run api POST /v1/queues/p3/purge
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$J/nack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"$T\",\"error\":\"after purge\"}"
  run jget $J
  run api POST /v1/queues/p3/purge
  run jget $J; }
P4() { echo "== P4 cancel->retry, dead->cancel, succeeded->retry $(ts)"
  run mkq p4 '"max_attempts":1'
  W=$(wk p4w)
  A=$(api POST /v1/queues/p4/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$A/cancel
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$A/retry
  B=$(api POST /v1/queues/p4/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  T=$(lease1 p4 $W | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r '.jobs[0].lease_token')
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$B/nack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"$T\",\"error\":\"x\"}"
  run jget $B
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$B/cancel
  C=$(api POST /v1/queues/p4/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  T=$(lease1 p4 $W | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r '.jobs[0].lease_token')
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$C/ack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"$T\",\"result\":1}"
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$C/retry
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$C/cancel; }
P5() { echo "== P5 lease, cancel: lease fields $(ts)"
  run mkq p5
  W=$(wk p5w)
  J=$(api POST /v1/queues/p5/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  run lease1 p5 $W
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$J/cancel
  run jget $J
  run api GET /v1/jobs/$J; }
P6() { echo "== P6 lease, delete worker, lease ... (max_attempts 2) $(ts)"
  run mkq p6 '"max_attempts":2'
  J=$(api POST /v1/queues/p6/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id); echo "job $J"
  for i in 1 2 3 4; do
    W=$(wk p6w$i)
    L=$(lease1 p6 $W); echo "lease by $W: $L"
    T=$(echo "$L" | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r '.jobs[0].lease_token')
    run api DELETE /v1/workers/$W
    run api POST /v1/jobs/$J/heartbeat -d "{\"lease_token\":\"$T\",\"extend_seconds\":30}"
    run jget $J
  done
  run api GET /v1/jobs/$J/attempts
  run sql "select event,worker,attempt from job_events where job_id=$J order by id"; }
P7() { echo "== P7 lease (lease_seconds 2, max 1), pause, expiry while paused $(ts)"
  run mkq p7 '"lease_seconds":2,"max_attempts":1'
  W=$(wk p7w)
  J=$(api POST /v1/queues/p7/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  run lease1 p7 $W
  run api POST /v1/queues/p7/pause
  sleep 4
  run jget $J
  run api GET /v1/jobs/$J/attempts; }
P8() { echo "== P8 cancel scheduled / cancel retry_wait, then time passes $(ts)"
  run mkq p8 '"backoff":{"kind":"linear","base_seconds":30}'
  W=$(wk p8w)
  A=$(api POST /v1/queues/p8/jobs -d '{"kind":"k","delay_seconds":30}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  B=$(api POST /v1/queues/p8/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .id)
  T=$(lease1 p8 $W | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r '.jobs[0].lease_token')
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$B/nack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"$T\",\"error\":\"x\"}"
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$A/cancel
  run api POST /v1/jobs/$B/cancel
  run adm POST /admin/clock -d '{"action":"advance","seconds":120}'
  sleep 3
  run jget $A; run jget $B
  run lease1 p8 $W; }
for p in "$@"; do $p; done
EOF

# E05 random walk: pick a noun, pick a verb, act, observe, check the rules (rules.md R3/R5/R34/R35/R37/R38 as I1-I13).
# Usage: bash walk.sh SEED STEPS   (needs the e05 stack; source of env: tools/e05env.sh)
# Replay: same SEED and STEPS against a stack where the queue name w<SEED> does not exist yet; bash $RANDOM is
# deterministic for a given seed, but responses (ids, tokens) depend on stack state, so the log records every op.
# Output: one line per step "step|op|args|http|body(trimmed)" plus "VIOLATION ..." lines on first sight of (inv,id).
set -u
source "$(dirname "$0")/tools/e05env.sh"
SEED=${1:?seed}; STEPS=${2:-150}; RANDOM=$SEED
Q=w$SEED; MAX=2
declare -A TOK GRANTS LASTATT CANCELLED SEEN
JOBS=(); WORKERS=(); STALE=()
call() { local out; out=$(api "$@"); CODE=${out##*[}; CODE=${CODE%]}; BODY=${out% \[*}; }
pick() { local -n arr=$1; [ ${#arr[@]} -gt 0 ] || return 1; echo "${arr[$((RANDOM % ${#arr[@]}))]}"; }
log() { echo "$STEP|$1|$2|$CODE|$(echo "$BODY" | tr -d '\n' | cut -c1-160)"; }
violation() { local key="$1:$2"; [ -n "${SEEN[$key]:-}" ] && return; SEEN[$key]=1; echo "VIOLATION step=$STEP inv=$1 job=$2 $3"; }
check() { # $1 = "tick" when the loop has had time to run after a clock change
  local now; now=$(adm POST /admin/clock -d '{"action":"advance","seconds":0}' | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .now)
  local extra=""
  [ "${1:-}" = tick ] && extra="UNION ALL SELECT 'I12',id,state FROM j WHERE state IN ('scheduled','retry_wait') AND run_at <= '$now'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'I13',id,state FROM j WHERE state='leased' AND lease_expires_at <= '$now'"
  while IFS='|' read -r inv id st; do
    inv=${inv// /}; id=${id// /}; st=${st// /}
    [ -n "$inv" ] && violation "$inv" "$id" "state=$st"
  done < <(PGPASSWORD=explorer psql -h localhost -p 15493 -U explorer -d queuelet -X -A -t -F'|' -c "
    WITH j AS (SELECT * FROM jobs WHERE queue_id=(SELECT id FROM queues WHERE name='$Q' AND namespace_id=1))
    SELECT 'I1',id,state FROM j WHERE state NOT IN ('scheduled','queued','leased','retry_wait','succeeded','dead','cancelled')
    UNION ALL SELECT 'I2',id,state FROM j WHERE (finished_at IS NOT NULL) <> (state IN ('succeeded','dead','cancelled'))
    UNION ALL SELECT 'I3',id,state FROM j WHERE attempts > max_attempts
    UNION ALL SELECT 'I5',a.job_id,'' FROM attempts a JOIN j ON j.id=a.job_id GROUP BY a.job_id HAVING count(*)<>max(a.n) OR count(DISTINCT a.n)<>count(*)
    UNION ALL SELECT CASE WHEN state='cancelled' THEN 'I7c' ELSE 'I7' END,id,state FROM j WHERE (state='leased') <> (lease_token IS NOT NULL AND leased_by IS NOT NULL AND lease_expires_at IS NOT NULL)
    UNION ALL SELECT 'I9',id,state FROM j WHERE state IN ('scheduled','retry_wait') AND run_at < event_at
    $extra")
  # I10 stats equal a direct count
  local s c; s=$(api GET /v1/queues/$Q/stats | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -c '{scheduled,queued,leased,retry_wait,succeeded,dead,cancelled}')
  c=$(PGPASSWORD=explorer psql -h localhost -p 15493 -U explorer -d queuelet -X -A -t -c "SELECT json_build_object('scheduled',count(*) FILTER (WHERE state='scheduled'),'queued',count(*) FILTER (WHERE state='queued'),'leased',count(*) FILTER (WHERE state='leased'),'retry_wait',count(*) FILTER (WHERE state='retry_wait'),'succeeded',count(*) FILTER (WHERE state='succeeded'),'dead',count(*) FILTER (WHERE state='dead'),'cancelled',count(*) FILTER (WHERE state='cancelled')) FROM jobs WHERE queue_id=(SELECT id FROM queues WHERE name='$Q' AND namespace_id=1)" | jq -c .)
  [ "$s" = "$c" ] || violation I10 q "stats=$s count=$c"
}
STEP=0; CODE=-; BODY=""
call POST /v1/queues -d "{\"name\":\"$Q\",\"lease_seconds\":20,\"max_attempts\":$MAX,\"backoff\":{\"kind\":\"linear\",\"base_seconds\":5}}"; log setup "queue $Q"
for i in 1 2; do call POST /v1/workers -d "{\"name\":\"$Q-w$i\",\"kinds\":[\"k\"]}"; WORKERS+=("$(echo "$BODY" | jq -r .worker_id)"); log setup worker; done
for STEP in $(seq 1 "$STEPS"); do
  r=$((RANDOM % 100)); tick=""
  if   [ $r -lt 12 ]; then call POST /v1/queues/$Q/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}'; JOBS+=("$(echo "$BODY" | jq -r .id)"); log job.enqueue now
  elif [ $r -lt 17 ]; then call POST /v1/queues/$Q/jobs -d '{"kind":"k","delay_seconds":15}'; JOBS+=("$(echo "$BODY" | jq -r .id)"); log job.enqueue delay15
  elif [ $r -lt 32 ]; then w=$(pick WORKERS) || { w=999999; }; n=$((1 + RANDOM % 3))
    call POST /v1/queues/$Q/lease -d "{\"worker_id\":$w,\"max_jobs\":$n}"; log lease.lease "w=$w n=$n"
    if [ "$CODE" = 200 ]; then
      while read -r id att tok; do [ -z "$id" ] && continue
        [ -n "${TOK[$id]:-}" ] && STALE+=("$id:${TOK[$id]}"); TOK[$id]=$tok
        GRANTS[$id]=$(( ${GRANTS[$id]:-0} + 1 ))
        [ -n "${CANCELLED[$id]:-}" ] && violation I6 "$id" "cancelled job leased"
        [ "${GRANTS[$id]}" -gt $MAX ] && violation I4 "$id" "grant ${GRANTS[$id]} > max $MAX (attempt=$att)"
        [ "$att" -le "${LASTATT[$id]:-0}" ] && violation I8 "$id" "attempt $att <= previous ${LASTATT[$id]}"
        LASTATT[$id]=$att
      done < <(echo "$BODY" | jq -r '.jobs[] | "\(.id) \(.attempt) \(.lease_token)"')
    fi
  elif [ $r -lt 42 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/ack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"${TOK[$j]:-none}\",\"result\":{\"s\":$STEP}}"; log job.ack "j=$j"
  elif [ $r -lt 50 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/nack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"${TOK[$j]:-none}\",\"error\":\"e$STEP\"}"; log job.nack "j=$j"
  elif [ $r -lt 53 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/nack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"${TOK[$j]:-none}\",\"error\":\"e$STEP\",\"retry\":false}"; log job.nack "j=$j retry=false"
  elif [ $r -lt 56 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/heartbeat -d "{\"lease_token\":\"${TOK[$j]:-none}\",\"extend_seconds\":20}"; log job.heartbeat "j=$j"
  elif [ $r -lt 59 ]; then s=$(pick STALE) || continue; j=${s%%:*}; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/ack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"${s#*:}\",\"result\":0}"; log job.ack "j=$j STALE token"
    [ "$CODE" = 200 ] && violation R2 "$j" "stale token ack accepted"
  elif [ $r -lt 65 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/cancel; log job.cancel "j=$j"; [ "$CODE" = 200 ] && CANCELLED[$j]=1
  elif [ $r -lt 71 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/retry; log job.retry "j=$j"
    [ "$CODE" = 200 ] && { GRANTS[$j]=0; LASTATT[$j]=0; }
  elif [ $r -lt 74 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call DELETE /v1/jobs/$j; log job.delete "j=$j"
  elif [ $r -lt 77 ]; then call POST /v1/queues/$Q/pause; log queue.pause ""
  elif [ $r -lt 81 ]; then call POST /v1/queues/$Q/resume; log queue.resume ""
  elif [ $r -lt 83 ]; then call POST /v1/queues/$Q/purge; log queue.purge ""
  elif [ $r -lt 86 ]; then call POST /v1/workers -d "{\"name\":\"$Q-s$STEP\",\"kinds\":[\"k\"]}"; WORKERS+=("$(echo "$BODY" | jq -r .worker_id)"); log worker.create ""
  elif [ $r -lt 90 ]; then [ ${#WORKERS[@]} -gt 0 ] || continue; k=$((RANDOM % ${#WORKERS[@]})); w=${WORKERS[$k]}
    call DELETE /v1/workers/$w; log worker.delete "w=$w"; [ "$CODE" = 200 ] && { unset 'WORKERS[k]'; WORKERS=("${WORKERS[@]}"); }
  else secs=$(( (RANDOM % 3 == 0) ? 25 : 6 )); out=$(adm POST /admin/clock -d "{\"action\":\"advance\",\"seconds\":$secs}"); CODE=${out##*[}; CODE=${CODE%]}; BODY=${out% \[*}
    log clock.advance "+$secs"; sleep 1.6; tick=tick
  fi
  check $tick
done
echo "SUMMARY seed=$SEED steps=$STEPS jobs=${#JOBS[@]} violations=${#SEEN[@]} keys=$(printf '%s ' "${!SEEN[@]}" | tr ' ' '\n' | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' ')"

  elif [ $r -lt 53 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/nack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"${TOK[$j]:-none}\",\"error\":\"e$STEP\",\"retry\":false}"; log job.nack "j=$j retry=false"
  elif [ $r -lt 56 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/heartbeat -d "{\"lease_token\":\"${TOK[$j]:-none}\",\"extend_seconds\":20}"; log job.heartbeat "j=$j"
  elif [ $r -lt 59 ]; then s=$(pick STALE) || continue; j=${s%%:*}; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/ack -d "{\"lease_token\":\"${s#*:}\",\"result\":0}"; log job.ack "j=$j STALE token"
    [ "$CODE" = 200 ] && violation R2 "$j" "stale token ack accepted"
  elif [ $r -lt 65 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/cancel; log job.cancel "j=$j"; [ "$CODE" = 200 ] && CANCELLED[$j]=1
  elif [ $r -lt 71 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call POST /v1/jobs/$j/retry; log job.retry "j=$j"
    [ "$CODE" = 200 ] && { GRANTS[$j]=0; LASTATT[$j]=0; }
  elif [ $r -lt 74 ]; then j=$(pick JOBS) || continue; call DELETE /v1/jobs/$j; log job.delete "j=$j"
  elif [ $r -lt 77 ]; then call POST /v1/queues/$Q/pause; log queue.pause ""
  elif [ $r -lt 81 ]; then call POST /v1/queues/$Q/resume; log queue.resume ""
  elif [ $r -lt 83 ]; then call POST /v1/queues/$Q/purge; log queue.purge ""
  elif [ $r -lt 86 ]; then call POST /v1/workers -d "{\"name\":\"$Q-s$STEP\",\"kinds\":[\"k\"]}"; WORKERS+=("$(echo "$BODY" | jq -r .worker_id)"); log worker.create ""
  elif [ $r -lt 90 ]; then [ ${#WORKERS[@]} -gt 0 ] || continue; k=$((RANDOM % ${#WORKERS[@]})); w=${WORKERS[$k]}
    call DELETE /v1/workers/$w; log worker.delete "w=$w"; [ "$CODE" = 200 ] && { unset 'WORKERS[k]'; WORKERS=("${WORKERS[@]}"); }
  else secs=$(( (RANDOM % 3 == 0) ? 25 : 6 )); out=$(adm POST /admin/clock -d "{\"action\":\"advance\",\"seconds\":$secs}"); CODE=${out##*[}; CODE=${CODE%]}; BODY=${out% \[*}
    log clock.advance "+$secs"; sleep 1.6; tick=tick
  fi
  check $tick
done

input.content:
# E05-F01 — Releasing a lease by deleting the worker hands the job out again under the same attempt number, without limit

Seen at: export of `explore-it/lesson-04` (stack `queuelet-e05`), experiment 05 (sequence-it).
Original observations: [E05 notes, P6](../experiments/05-sequence-it/notes.md) (13:23:10Z), isolation H-E05-11/12
(13:24:41Z), random walk seed 11 steps 26→78 and 133→136/146 ([walk log](../experiments/05-sequence-it/notes.md)).

## Minimal reproduction

Actor: one namespace key (acme). Clock: any (observed both on the real clock and with the test clock frozen). No
compose worker involved (queue name not polled).

```sh
source exploration/experiments/05-sequence-it/tools/e05env.sh
api POST /v1/queues -d '{"name":"p6","max_attempts":2}'
api POST /v1/queues/p6/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}'                         # job 8
for i in 1 2 3 4; do
  W=$(api POST /v1/workers -d "{\"name\":\"p6w$i\",\"kinds\":[\"k\"]}" | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .worker_id)
  api POST /v1/queues/p6/lease -d "{\"worker_id\":$W,\"max_jobs\":1}"  # "attempt":1 every time
  api DELETE /v1/workers/$W                                            # 200, job back to queued
done
api GET /v1/jobs/8/attempts                                            # {"attempts":[]}
```

Replay script: `exploration/experiments/05-sequence-it/tools/pairs.sh P6`; variants `tools/isolate.sh`.

## Expected (named oracle)

SPEC "Worker protocol": *"No job may execute more than its maximum attempts."* SPEC "Jobs": *"Attempt `n` numbers every
execution of the job and is never reused …; the lease's `attempt` counts toward `max_attempts`."* rules.md R3/R32 (Never
rule). Comparable system (recalled, not verified in this run): SQS increments `ApproximateReceiveCount` on every receive,
and the redrive policy's `maxReceiveCount` counts receives regardless of how the message became visible again.

So each lease handed out should consume an attempt (or the release should otherwise be counted): with max_attempts 2, a
third delivery must not happen, and two deliveries must not both be told `attempt: 1`.

## Observed

| Variant | Deliveries observed | Lease `attempt` values | `attempts` column | attempts history |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| max 2, fresh job (P6, job 8) | 4 (workers 6, 7, 8, 9) | 1, 1, 1, 1 | 0 | `[]` |
| max 3 after one nack (H-E05-11, job 13) | 3 (w13, w14, w15) | 1, 2, **2** | 1 | n1 failed only |
| max **1** (H-E05-12, job 14) | 2 (w16, w17) then nack → dead | 1, 1 | 1 | n1 failed (w17) only |
| walk seed 11, max 2 (jobs 21, 24, 25) | 3 each | job 21: 1, 1, 2, 2 | ≤ 2 | expiry rows only |

`job_events` for job 8: `created | leased 6 (1) | queued 6 (0) | leased 7 (1) | queued 7 (0) | leased 8 (1) | queued 8 (0) |
leased 9 (1) | queued 9 (0)` — the only place the deliveries appear.

Source route (code reading, consistent with the runtime): `internal/api/jobs.go:126` releases with
`UPDATE jobs SET state='queued',…,run_at=$2,lease_token=NULL,leased_by=NULL,lease_expires_at=NULL` — `attempts` unchanged
and no `attempts` row; `internal/jobs/jobs.go:77` reports `attempt = attempts+1`. Contrast `expire.go:116-120`, which for the
same "holder is gone" situation increments `attempts`, records an `expired` row and dead-letters at max.

## Variables isolated

- Matters: a `DELETE /v1/workers/{id}` while the worker holds the lease. Nothing else between the leases (no expiry,
  no nack) in P6.
- Does not matter: max_attempts (1, 2, 3); whether earlier counted attempts exist (H-E05-11 reuses attempt 2); real
  vs frozen test clock; how many jobs the worker holds (walk step 133 released three jobs at once, all reused).
- Old holder's token after release: heartbeat 409 (P6 ×4) — the lease *is* revoked; the issue is only accounting.
- Not tried: a worker process that deregisters itself on shutdown (the sample worker in `cmd/worker` does not call
  DELETE — grep found no deregistration), so the realistic trigger is operator cleanup or a third-party worker that
  deregisters on SIGTERM while executing.

## Sibling search

Predicted before probing (notes 13:24:30Z, H-E05-13): other release/exit paths. Checked:

- `expire.go:116` — counts (P7: max 1 → dead with `expired` row). Not a sibling.
- `nack.go:60` — counts. Not a sibling.
- `operator.go:6` Cancel of a leased job — no attempt row for the in-flight delivery (H-E05-14), but the job is terminal
  and cannot run again, so no budget bypass; reported with its lease-field symptom in
  [E05-F02](E05-F02-terminal-rows-keep-lease-fields.md).
- `operator.go:13` Retry resets attempts by design (SPEC: "resets its attempt count").
- Event console mislabels this release as `lease_expired` once the row's `last_error` is "lease expired":
  [E05-F03](E05-F03-worker-release-logged-as-lease-expired.md).

## Severity and status

Severity: **medium-high**. A poison job whose workers are deregistered while running (operator cleanup of stuck workers,

# E05-F01 — Releasing a lease by deleting the worker hands the job out again under the same attempt number, without limit

Seen at: export of `explore-it/lesson-04` (stack `queuelet-e05`), experiment 05 (sequence-it).
Original observations: [E05 notes, P6](../experiments/05-sequence-it/notes.md) (13:23:10Z), isolation H-E05-11/12
(13:24:41Z), random walk seed 11 steps 26→78 and 133→136/146 ([walk log](../experiments/05-sequence-it/notes.md)).

## Minimal reproduction

Actor: one namespace key (acme). Clock: any (observed both on the real clock and with the test clock frozen). No
compose worker involved (queue name not polled).

```sh
source exploration/experiments/05-sequence-it/tools/e05env.sh
api POST /v1/queues -d '{"name":"p6","max_attempts":2}'
api POST /v1/queues/p6/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}'                         # job 8
for i in 1 2 3 4; do
  W=$(api POST /v1/workers -d "{\"name\":\"p6w$i\",\"kinds\":[\"k\"]}" | sed 's/ \[.*//' | jq -r .worker_id)
  api POST /v1/queues/p6/lease -d "{\"worker_id\":$W,\"max_jobs\":1}"  # "attempt":1 every time
  api DELETE /v1/workers/$W                                            # 200, job back to queued
done
api GET /v1/jobs/8/attempts                                            # {"attempts":[]}
```

Replay script: `exploration/experiments/05-sequence-it/tools/pairs.sh P6`; variants `tools/isolate.sh`.

## Expected (named oracle)

SPEC "Worker protocol": *"No job may execute more than its maximum attempts."* SPEC "Jobs": *"Attempt `n` numbers every
execution of the job and is never reused …; the lease's `attempt` counts toward `max_attempts`."* rules.md R3/R32 (Never
rule). Comparable system (recalled, not verified in this run): SQS increments `ApproximateReceiveCount` on every receive,
and the redrive policy's `maxReceiveCount` counts receives regardless of how the message became visible again.

So each lease handed out should consume an attempt (or the release should otherwise be counted): with max_attempts 2, a
third delivery must not happen, and two deliveries must not both be told `attempt: 1`.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| max 2, fresh job (P6, job 8) | 4 (workers 6, 7, 8, 9) | 1, 1, 1, 1 | 0 | `[]` |
| max 3 after one nack (H-E05-11, job 13) | 3 (w13, w14, w15) | 1, 2, **2** | 1 | n1 failed only |
| max **1** (H-E05-12, job 14) | 2 (w16, w17) then nack → dead | 1, 1 | 1 | n1 failed (w17) only |
| walk seed 11, max 2 (jobs 21, 24, 25) | 3 each | job 21: 1, 1, 2, 2 | ≤ 2 | expiry rows only |

leased 9 (1) | queued 9 (0)` — the only place the deliveries appear.

`UPDATE jobs SET state='queued',…,run_at=$2,lease_token=NULL,leased_by=NULL,lease_expires_at=NULL` — `attempts` unchanged
and no `attempts` row; `internal/jobs/jobs.go:77` reports `attempt = attempts+1`. Contrast `expire.go:116-120`, which for the
same "holder is gone" situation increments `attempts`, records an `expired` row and dead-letters at max.

## Variables isolated

- Matters: a `DELETE /v1/workers/{id}` while the worker holds the lease. Nothing else between the leases (no expiry,
  no nack) in P6.

  vs frozen test clock; how many jobs the worker holds (walk step 133 released three jobs at once, all reused).

- Not tried: a worker process that deregisters itself on shutdown (the sample worker in `cmd/worker` does not call
  DELETE — grep found no deregistration), so the realistic trigger is operator cleanup or a third-party worker that
  deregisters on SIGTERM while executing.

Predicted before probing (notes 13:24:30Z, H-E05-13): other release/exit paths. Checked:

- `operator.go:6` Cancel of a leased job — no attempt row for the in-flight delivery (H-E05-14), but the job is terminal
  and cannot run again, so no budget bypass; reported with its lease-field symptom in
  [E05-F02](E05-F02-terminal-rows-keep-lease-fields.md).

- Event console mislabels this release as `lease_expired` once the row's `last_error` is "lease expired":
  [E05-F03](E05-F03-worker-release-logged-as-lease-expired.md).

Severity: **medium-high**. A poison job whose workers are deregistered while running (operator cleanup of stuck workers,
autoscaler scale-in that deregisters) is redelivered forever and never reaches `dead`; every redelivery is reported to
the worker as the same attempt number, and the attempts API shows none of them, so the retry budget and the history both
understate execution. Breaks a SPEC Never rule.

Status: `open`.

# E05-F03 — The event console reports a worker-deletion release as `lease_expired` when an earlier lease had expired

Seen at: export of `explore-it/lesson-04` (stack `queuelet-e05`), experiment 05 (sequence-it).
Original observation: walk seed 11, job 21 event 134 (notes 13:26:45Z); minimal reproduction H-E05-15 (13:32:08Z,
raw `project/results/e05/f02-f03.txt`).

## Minimal reproduction

Actor: acme key. Clock: test clock frozen; advanced explicitly (`/admin/clock`, admin key).

```sh
source exploration/experiments/05-sequence-it/tools/e05env.sh   # replay: tools/f02.sh (first block)
api POST /v1/queues -d '{"name":"f3","lease_seconds":2,"max_attempts":5}'
api POST /v1/queues/f3/jobs -d '{"kind":"k"}'                            # job 108
# worker 52 leases (attempt 1); advance clock 3 s; loop expires it -> queued, attempts 1, last_error "lease expired"
# worker 53 leases (attempt 2, lease_expires_at 14:35:40); clock still 14:35:38; DELETE /v1/workers/53 -> 200
api GET /v1/jobs/108/events
```

Observed events (API and identical `job event` lines in `docker compose logs api`):

```
{"id":336,"at":"14:35:38.41404Z","event":"lease_expired","worker":52,"attempt":1,"error":"lease expired"}   # real expiry
{"id":337,"at":"14:35:38.41404Z","event":"leased","worker":53,"attempt":2,"error":"lease expired"}
{"id":338,"at":"14:35:38.41404Z","event":"lease_expired","worker":53,"attempt":1,"error":"lease expired"}   # worker deleted
```

Event 338 is the release caused by `DELETE /v1/workers/53` while worker 53's lease still had 2 s to run.

## Expected (named oracle)

The event console's own contract (migrations/002.sql comment "Observation only"; SPEC Notifications/operations exposes
`/v1/jobs/{id}/events` as job history) — an event label names the transition that happened. Control: the same release
without a prior expiry is labelled `queued` (P6: `leased 6 | queued 6 | …`). Consistency approximation: the same API
call must produce the same label regardless of an earlier, unrelated error text.

## Observed vs predicted

Predicted from the trigger before the probe (H-E05-15): `observe_job()` labels `lease_expired` when
`OLD.state='leased' AND NEW.last_error='lease expired'`; `internal/api/jobs.go:126` keeps `last_error` from the earlier
expiry. Observed as predicted. Also the `attempt` column drops from 2 (leased) to 1 on the "expired" event, while a real
expiry would show attempts+1 — a reader sees an expiry that consumed no attempt.

## Variables isolated

- Matters: the job's `last_error` is exactly `lease expired` (from an earlier expiry) when the worker is deleted.
- Does not matter: whether the earlier expired lease belonged to the same worker (52 vs 53 here).
- Control without prior expiry: label `queued` (P6, four times).
- Not tried: a job whose last nack error text is literally `lease expired` (any worker can send that text; same
  trigger condition, so the label would follow — prediction only).

## Sibling search

Same trigger, other writers that leave `leased` while `last_error` may already be `lease expired`:
`ack.go:25` (state changes to `succeeded`, so label is `succeeded` — not a sibling: the CASE tests `NEW.last_error` only
when… no, it tests it for any state change from leased; an ack of a job whose previous attempt expired sets state
succeeded but keeps last_error `lease expired`). **Prediction, unprobed**: ack after an earlier expiry is logged as
`lease_expired`. Cancel of a leased job with a prior expiry likewise. Recorded as H-E05-18 (open).

## Severity and status

Severity: **low–medium** (observability). An operator reading history to diagnose E05-F01-style redelivery or a crashed
worker is told the lease expired, pointing at lease duration instead of the deregistration. No state effect.

Status: `open`.

# Experiment 05 — sequence-it: revealed

Build: plain export of `explore-it/lesson-04`, isolated stack `queuelet-e05` (API :18260, PG :15493, test clock on).
Explorer: fresh headless Claude Opus 5.5 session. Record: [notes.md](notes.md); walker: [walk.sh](walk.sh); helpers in
[tools/](tools/); raw output in `project/results/e05/`.

## Status

**done.** The charter's prediction ("every verb either does what it says from any starting point or is refused") was
refuted by the fourth probe: a job with `max_attempts` 2 was handed to four workers, each told it was attempt 1.

## Elapsed

13:17:51Z → about 13:46Z, roughly 28 minutes of the 60-minute budget.

| Activity | Minutes (approx.) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Reading | 5 | STATE, charter, protocol, skill, SPEC, models, lesson 04, the lifecycle source (13:17:51–13:21:30, plus short reads during the run) |
| Probing | 13 | directed pairs and triples 13:22:22–13:24:41; walks and minimal reproductions 13:26:45–13:40:11 (about 5 min of that was spent waiting on background walks while I wrote reports) |
| Writing | 10 | predictions before each probe, three defect reports, models, this file |

## What the system showed

- **Worker deregistration bypasses the retry budget.** `DELETE /v1/workers/{id}` puts the worker's leased jobs back in
  `queued` without counting an attempt and without writing to the attempts history. The next lease reports the same
  attempt number. This can repeat without limit: 4 deliveries on max 2 (P6), 2 deliveries on max 1 (H-E05-12), and attempt 2
  handed out twice after a real failure (H-E05-11). In walk seed 32, job 212 ran four times before it went `dead` on
  max 2. Lease expiry and nack, which the code treats as the same "holder gone" situation, both count the attempt.
  → [E05-F01](../../defects/E05-F01-worker-delete-release-uncounted-attempt.md)
- **Ack and cancel leave a live-looking lease on terminal jobs.** `succeeded` and `cancelled` rows keep `lease_token`,
  `leased_by` and an unexpired `lease_expires_at`, and `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` returns them. A job cancelled while leased
  has no attempt row for that delivery, and it keeps naming its worker after that worker is deleted. Nack, expiry and
  worker release all clear these fields.
  → [E05-F02](../../defects/E05-F02-terminal-rows-keep-lease-fields.md)
- **After one lease expiry, the event history mislabels later exits from `leased`.** Ack (to `succeeded`), cancel and
  worker release are all logged as `lease_expired`, in both `/v1/jobs/{id}/events` and the API log. The trigger decides
  on the sticky `last_error` text.
  → [E05-F03](../../defects/E05-F03-worker-release-logged-as-lease-expired.md)
- **What held:**
  - purge → enqueue with the same idempotency key (P1);
  - purge skips a leased job, and a later nack sends it to `retry_wait` (P3);
  - cancel/retry/terminal combinations return 409 (P4);
  - pause blocks leases, does not stop expiry or promotion, and produces no catch-up burst after +1 h and resume (P2, P7);
  - cancelled scheduled and retry_wait jobs stay cancelled past their due time (P8);
  - a released holder's token gets 409 (P6);
  - across 950 random-walk steps (5 completed seeds), no violation of I1, I2, I3, I5, I6, I9, I10, I12, I13 or the
    stale-token rule.
- **Surprises that are not defects:**
  - Every clock `advance` or `set` freezes semantic time (clock.go:182-191). This is documented lab behaviour, recorded
    as testability request T-E05-1.
  - A dead job keeps a future `run_at`. No reader uses it.
  - A scheduled job is promoted to `queued` while its queue is paused. It cannot be leased, so nothing is delivered.
  - A leased job survives purge. It is not "pending" in the SPEC's sense.
  - `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` exposes the live lease token to the whole namespace. Saved as `#offcharter`, not judged.

## Model delta

- [states.md](../../models/states.md), E05 revision: lifecycle diagram for the five exits from `leased` and the pause
  arrows, plus 18 starred state/event cells (should, predicted, observed).
- [rules.md](../../models/rules.md), E05 revision: invariants I1–I13 as walk checks, new rules R44–R48, and outcomes for
  R2, R3, R5 and R6.
- [nouns-verbs.md](../../models/nouns-verbs.md), E05 revision: the sequence grid (directed pairs/triples and walks) and
  the sequences still untested.
- [causes.md](../../models/causes.md): C25 (each exit from `leased` decides on its own which columns to reset) and C26
  (observation keyed on sticky error text), with timestamped sibling predictions.
- [hypotheses.md](../../hypotheses.md): H-E05-C, H-E05-01 to H-E05-21, Q-E05-1/2, T-E05-1 and one `#offcharter` item.

## Unresolved and next hypotheses

- **Q-E05-1 (owner):** should a release by worker deregistration count as an attempt, or be recorded as a distinct
  release with its own cap?
- **Q-E05-2 (owner):** should a terminal row keep `leased_by` (who completed it) while clearing the token and expiry?
- **H-E05-20:** a nack whose error text is exactly `lease expired` will be logged as an expiry (not probed).
- **H-E05-21:** a worker that deregisters on SIGTERM while executing turns a crash-looping poison job into unbounded
  redelivery (ecosystem).
- **T-E05-1:** add an "offset and keep ticking" clock mode so clock jumps and real-time lease expiry can be combined.
- **Walker coverage limits:**
  - Successful holder verbs were rare in the uniform walks (0–4 acks per seed). Holder-biased v2 raised this to 7 and 12.
  - Operator retry succeeded only 6 times in all walks.
  - Schedules, queue DELETE, retention and webhooks were not part of the walk.
  - One rejected or skipped operation is not coverage of the success arrow.
- **Dead ends kept:**
  - The seed-1 smoke run crashed on `set -u`.
  - Seed 21 starved: no workers left and the queue paused about half the time.
  - My broad `pkill -f walk.sh` also killed my own shell and stopped seed 22.

## Score

| Measure | Count | Evidence / counting basis |
|---|---|---|
| Hypotheses stated | 22 | H-E05-C, H-E05-01 … H-E05-21, each written in notes before its probe (13:22:19Z, 13:24:30Z, 13:29:40Z, 13:34Z, 13:33Z). H-E05-20/21 are backlog, not probed. Invariants I1–I13 are rules, not counted here |
| Hypotheses confirmed | 18 | H-E05-01…09, 11…19 (P1–P8, isolate.txt, f02-f03.txt, f03-sibling.txt, walk-b31/b32.txt). H-E05-19 is confirmed on its stated refutation condition; its coverage sub-prediction missed for seed 31 |
| Hypotheses refuted | 2 | H-E05-C (P6, E05-F01); H-E05-10 (I7 fired on succeeded rows, walk-11 step 24) |
| Code-reading predictions contradicted by the running system | 2 | H-E05-C (handler reading); H-E05-10 (I had read ack.go:25 and predicted I7 for cancel only) |
| Defects found | 3 | [E05-F01](../../defects/E05-F01-worker-delete-release-uncounted-attempt.md), [E05-F02](../../defects/E05-F02-terminal-rows-keep-lease-fields.md), [E05-F03](../../defects/E05-F03-worker-release-logged-as-lease-expired.md). Repeated walk hits of the same causes are counted once; regressions that held (F06/R6, F25 purge, E04-F04 token-after-expiry) are not counted |
| Model cells filled | 16 | States E05 table: 18 starred cells, minus 2 revisits already observed earlier (cancelled→retry in E04 P5; succeeded→retry in E01 F06) |
| Open | 2 | H-E05-20, H-E05-21 (not probed) |
